From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-16T08:42:00Z
Subject: MAP: Routing resiliency metrics & close cadence (regional latency validation)

Michael / Selina —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our MAP, attached is a focused execution plan for the regional latency and failover validation you'll need to sign off before we can finalize the Dedicated capacity commitment. High level: we want to validate TTFT, steady-state throughput and concurrency, and measure cross-region failover time (US <-> EU and US <-> APAC) under your expected traffic profile.

Planned test windows (tentative):
- Week 1 (Apr 19-21): Baseline single-region latency and TTFT (US-east).
- Week 2 (Apr 22-24): Multi-region routing + weighted traffic (EU/US/APAC) to measure routing latencies and non-preferred-region penalties.
- Week 3 (Apr 26): Failover exercises with simulated zone outage and warm fallback to secondary region.

Key success criteria (what BrightHealth needs to accept):
- Median generation latency (per-token) within target for P95 <= 220ms for 1-2k token prompts.
- TTFT (time to first token) P95 <= 180ms under 50 concurrent sessions.
- Sustained throughput: 600 tokens/sec per reserved GPU cluster slice at 75% CPU/GPU utilization.
- Failover RTO (route update + traffic stabilization) < 45s for region switch; no more than 1% error spike.

I've attached the routing playbook and an initial csv of last-run latency samples from our lab environment. Please review and confirm availability for the test windows. If we get sign-off this week, our legal/procurement teams have what they need to push the contract to final signatures by Apr 30 — matching the close cadence we discussed.

Next steps for BrightHealth:
1) Confirm attendance and primary contacts for ops and security (names + emails).
2) Confirm which data residency rules we should enforce during the tests (if any sample payloads must be anonymized).
3) Approve the proposed test windows or provide alternates.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Principal Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Jordan —

Thanks for the detailed plan. We like the staged approach. A few clarifying questions before we confirm windows: 

1) When you reference "P95 <= 220ms for 1-2k token prompts" — is that measured from our public API edge or from the private VPC endpoint? We need to understand exposure to our internal network SMT.
2) For the failover exercises, can you confirm whether the failover involves DNS-level re-routing or an L4 proxy-level shift? Our infra team prefers not to change DNS TTLs during the exercise.
3) Can Redwood add a smoke test that validates session affinity for long-running chat contexts (30+ minutes) so we can ensure KV cache continuity on failover?

Also, our procurement lead is out until Apr 20 — so if you need final signatures before Apr 30 we'll likely have to compress approvals. Can Redwood accommodate a short grace period for final PO issuance?

I'll get OPS+SEC contact names to you by tomorrow.

-Michael
Michael Turner
Director of Platform Engineering | BrightHealth
michael.turner@brighthealth.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-17T09:21:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP: Routing resiliency metrics & close cadence (regional latency validation)

Michael —

Thanks — good questions. Quick answers inline, and added a technical note from Karthik below for the failover mechanics.

1) Measurement point: by default the CSV attached is from our public-hosted edge (0.3ms internal network excluded). For Dedicated/VPC tests we'll instrument both the public edge and the private tunnel endpoint; final acceptance will use the private endpoint numbers you see in the test harness.

2) Failover mechanics: we can run both modes. For the MAP exercises we recommend proxy-level (L4) weighted traffic shift to avoid DNS TTL churn. Karthik: please see the short note on session affinity and routing below.

3) Session affinity smoke test: noted — we'll include a 30-minute chat context continuity test during Week 3; the plan will snapshot KV cache hit rates before/after failover and reproduce a 30-minute conversation to validate continuity.

Procurement: we can extend the internal signoff window to May 7 if that helps — we'll mark the deal close target as soft May 7, firm May 14 subject to PO receipt. Laura, can you confirm we are comfortable with that cadence?

Karthik's note (copied):
> From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
> Date: 2027-04-17T09:05:00Z
>
> For clarity on routing/failover: our recommended approach for tests is to use our smart routing agent which can perform sub-60s failover without DNS changes. The agent updates our control-plane routing table and signals the edge proxies to drain/shift connections. For session affinity we maintain KV cache replication across regions with a two-way async replication; we will measure eventual consistency windows in the smoke test. If BrightHealth needs strict zero-loss affinity we can run an active-active sticky mode but that will increase cross-region egress by ~8-12%.

Attaching a short ddos_test_notes.txt that describes how we emulate partial region degradation (simulated instance failure + controlled packet loss) and the CSV contains last night's lab run (baseline numbers across three regions).

Jordan
